name: Ween
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Two guys and a DAT machine out of New Hope, Pennsylvania, made a soul record, a country record and a sea record, and nobody ever worked out when they were joking.

eras.title: Cassettes nobody asked for
eras.text: Two kids who don't like each other end up in the same class in New Hope, Pennsylvania, and spend five years making cassettes. By the end of the decade they're opening for the Butthole Surfers at Trenton's City Gardens and a Twin/Tone scout has noticed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Typing class pairs two kids who can't stand each other
years.p: Aaron Freeman and Mickey Melchiondo land in the same junior high class in New Hope, Pennsylvania. They become Gene Ween and Dean Ween.
years.xp:
Freeman put it plainly: "We didn't like each other. He was a jock, and I was more of a trench-coat guy." Per Wikipedia, the band name mashes together the words "wuss" and "penis".

Four years of self-released cassettes followed, including Mrs. Slack (1984), Erica Peterson's Flaming Crib Death (1986), The Crucial Squeegie Lip (1987) and Axis: Bold as Boognish (1988). Their public debut, in 1986, was a Jimi Hendrix cover at the New Hope-Solebury High School talent show, with Chris Williams on bass and Karl Weimer on drums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: New Hope's John and Peter's is home; Trenton's City Gardens is the big room
years.p: By 1988 Gene and Dean are regulars at both, and the acts they open for include the Butthole Surfers and They Might Be Giants.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]] and [[They Might Be Giants|183d6ef6-e161-47ff-9085-063c8b897e97]] among the acts Ween opened for. Meanwhile Dean was publishing a fanzine called Yuck and working the Trenton punk scene, Magnet reports.

The live act was two guys, two guitars and a DAT machine playing the backing tracks. That was the whole band until 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: Twin/Tone signs a band with no drummer
years.p: A&R man Dave Ayers gets Ween onto Minneapolis indie Twin/Tone. Wikipedia says he caught them opening for Skunk in Maplewood, New Jersey.
years.xp: Magnet tells it differently: Twin/Tone signed them after a summer 1988 party show in New Jersey. Either way, Ayers ended up managing them as well.

eras.title: A bong-headed Leonard Cohen, then a major label
eras.text: The first record is on Twin/Tone, the second is on Kramer's label, and by the end of 1992 Elektra has them. Along the way a Fugazi crowd boos them.

years.src: The Varsity: A conversation with Dean Ween from 1996 · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: About 1,200 people boo Ween at a Fugazi show
years.p: Dean says it was the worst reception the band ever got.
years.xp:
Dean told The Varsity in 1996 that around 1,200 people booed the set at a [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] show. The source doesn't pin the date beyond about 1989 to 1990.

That February 1990, per Wikipedia, [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] faced a cool City Gardens crowd after Ween's set and told them to "start liking them now".

years.src: Wikipedia: GodWeenSatan: The Oneness · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Twin/Tone releases the debut, GodWeenSatan: The Oneness
years.p: Twenty-six tracks from the first six years; "You Fucked Up" and "Fat Lenny" become live staples.
years.xp:
Dean later called the album a greatest-hits collection. [[Andrew Weiss|afdb875c-cca9-4556-87c1-62f635688b13]] produced, and it was cut in 1989 and 1990 at places including the Zion House of Flesh in Hopewell, New Jersey. Ween's first overseas shows followed in the Netherlands, from December 1990 into January 1991.

Pitchfork later gave it a 9.6; Robert Christgau was less impressed.

years.cap: Gene and Dean Ween at Wetlands Preserve, New York, 1991
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pod · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: The Pod comes out on [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]]'s Shimmy-Disc, not Twin/Tone
years.p: Recorded on a Tascam four-track in the duo's apartment on Van Sant Road, Solebury Township.
years.xp:
The sessions ran January to October 1990. The cover parodies Leonard Cohen's The Best of Leonard Cohen, with Chris Williams's head, bong and all, over Cohen's. Wikipedia says both members had mononucleosis while recording, and the band dismissed drug theories as "the most slime-bag thing we could think of".

Magnet reports Kramer paid them $2,500 and took them to Jamaica, and quotes Dean on the label situation: "We breached our contract, which only a 19- or 20-year-old would have the balls to do." Weiss produced and mixed. After the first US and UK tours they recorded for John Peel at the BBC in February 1992. Aphex Twin later listed The Pod among his ten favorite albums, Wikipedia says; Elektra reissued it in 1995.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Guava · Wikipedia: Dean Ween
yt: Push th' Little Daisies, official video
years.h: Elektra releases Pure Guava, which still sounds like a home tape
years.p: It sells 65,000 copies in its first six months, per Wikipedia, and the four-track Ween is now on a major label.
years.xp: Guy Heller of [[Moistboyz|3867cba4-766a-4646-befd-010d053551ad]] sings lead on "Flies on My Dick"; Dean and Heller had started Moistboyz in 1991. "Big Jilm" was inspired by a car dealership employee named James A. Lemons, and "Poop Ship Destroyer" grew into a live jam vehicle.

eras.title: MTV lets them in, and a real band shows up
eras.text: Beavis and Butt-Head give Ween an actual hit, the DAT machine retires, and a fierce live band shows up. Then comes a soul album, and a country album Elektra didn't see coming.

years.cap: Ween at the Charlotte, Leicester, UK, 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Guava · Wikipedia: Ween
yt: Beavis and Butt-Head watch Push th' Little Daisies
years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head watch "Push th' Little Daisies"
years.p: MTV plays the clip heavily, and after a 1993 tour of Australia the single climbs to number 18 there.
years.xp: The radio edit swaps the profanity for a sample of Prince's squeal from "Alphabet St.", according to Wikipedia. The song was a US radio hit and an Australian success after the band toured there.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: Claude Coleman Jr. takes the drum stool and Andrew Weiss picks up a bass
years.p: After ten years of two guitars and a DAT machine, Ween has a rhythm section. Weiss, who produced the records, plays bass.
years.xp: Magnet says the pair turned Ween into a live band that could play three-hour shows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chocolate and Cheese · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Chocolate and Cheese is the first Ween record cut in a real studio
years.p: Weiss produces a pile-up of soul, funk and lounge, and Spike Jonze directs the video for "Freedom of '76".
years.xp:
"Roses Are Free" started turning up in [[Phish|e01646f2-2a04-450d-8bf2-0d993082e058]] setlists in 1997, and Ween started playing it more in response. Gene's verdict on jam bands, printed in Wikipedia: "all that jam band shit makes me want to puke."

About a month earlier they appeared in the Saturday Night Live film It's Pat, which was pulled from theaters a week after opening. In January 1995 they played "I Can't Put My Finger On It" on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.src: The Varsity: A conversation with Dean Ween from 1996 · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween makes a country album in Nashville
years.p: Cut in November 1995 under [[Ben Vaughn|d7a2fd5e-783a-4d5c-893d-4d3fbf249812]] with Nashville session players. The title promises twelve songs; the record has ten.
years.xp: Elektra had no idea a country album was coming, Dean told The Varsity: they just "handed it in". The Jordanaires sing on "I'm Holding You" and "Powder Blue".

eras.title: The sea record, and a goodbye to Elektra
eras.text: A five-piece lineup forms that lasts fifteen years. South Park calls, SpongeBob calls, and Ween leaves the major label.

years.h: Dave Dreiwitz and Glenn McClelland debut on Comedy Central
years.p: They play "The Golden Eel" on Viva Variety, on bass and keys. This lineup holds until 2012.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Mollusk · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: The Mollusk sets out to sea with shanties, Brit-pop and prog
years.p: Cut in 1996 and 1997 at studios including The Flood Zone in Holgate, New Jersey. Dean calls it "my favorite record we've ever done".
years.xp: Reviews split: Pitchfork gave it a 9.7, Entertainment Weekly a C, NME a 2 out of 10. Dean told Magnet an A&R executive left the finished album on his desk for two weeks unheard. Kurt Vile later named "Mutilated Lips" his favorite song ever.

years.src: Wikipedia: White Pepper · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: White Pepper is a pop album, and Ween's last for Elektra
years.p: [[Trey Parker|b8e4771f-6156-48cd-ab77-d10bc3fd50d9]] and [[Matt Stone|8b4844b3-70d6-4507-bc3f-85d09a8e35cd]] of South Park direct the "Even If You Don't" video. The album sells 72,000 copies in the US by November 2002, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Ween had already given Parker and Stone "Love" for Orgazmo in 1997 and "The Rainbow" for the South Park episode "Chef Aid" in 1998. Dean says they're "good friends"; Gene calls them "kindred spirits".

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: The Mollusk · Wikipedia: Ocean Man
years.h: SpongeBob's creator asks Ween for a song
years.p: Stephen Hillenburg cites The Mollusk as an inspiration; "Loop de Loop" plays in the episode "Your Shoe's Untied".
years.xp: "Ocean Man" closes The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie in 2004. In late 2015 and early 2016 an internet meme put the song over other movies' end credits, and Wikipedia says it became Ween's most-listened track on Spotify and Apple Music.

eras.title: After Elektra, a run of bad luck
eras.text: Ween starts its own label, Chocodog, loses its drummer to a car accident, makes Quebec as Gene's marriage ends, and cancels a tour for rehab.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween play GodWeenSatan front to back, as a duo
years.p: At John and Peter's in New Hope, to mark the album's reissue, Gene and Dean go back to two guitars and the DAT machine. Taping is banned.
years.xp: The show came out in 2016 as GodWeenSatan Live. That same year, 2001, Ween formed Chocodog Records, whose first release was the website-only Live in Toronto CD from their October 1996 tour with the Shit Creek Boys.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Quebec (album)
years.h: Claude Coleman breaks his back in a car accident on Route 78
years.p: Near Newark he also breaks his pelvis. Ween play benefit shows at the Bowery Ballroom in New York on October 7 and 8.
years.xp: [[Josh Freese|1ba97964-8d70-4b33-a361-d1a4ed222672]] of the Vandals filled in on those shows and on the next album. Coleman was back for an acoustic set in Brooklyn in December, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Quebec (album)
years.h: Quebec arrives as Gene's marriage ends
years.p: Ween's first album in three years is on Sanctuary, with [[Josh Freese|1ba97964-8d70-4b33-a361-d1a4ed222672]] on drums. Gene says most of the songs were written just before the marriage ended.
years.xp:
Dean's own take, quoted in Wikipedia: "I don't listen to any of our records, but I have never listened to that one." The Wikipedia page for the album also notes Dean was struggling with substance abuse during the sessions. Dean tells a story of cutting a guitar solo on Carlos Santana's gear in a shipping facility in ten minutes "without getting caught".

In November 2003 came All Request Live, a studio set chosen by fan vote that includes all five parts of "The Stallion".

years.h: Live in Chicago films the Quebec tour at the Vic Theatre
years.p: Shot in November 2003 and released in 2004 as a CD and DVD.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween cancel a Midwest tour so Gene can enter alcohol rehab
years.p: Manager Greg Frey's reason, given after a San Diego show. Ween stay off the road for a year.
years.xp: Frey's statement said the problem "requires immediate intervention, for the health, welfare, and safety of one of its members". Ween came back in October 2005.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: La Cucaracha is the last studio album, out on Rounder
years.p: Gene will later call it "a big piece of shit" and place the sessions at the point when he and Dean were "finito".
years.xp: Earlier, in Magnet, Gene had said the record was "going to dwarf everything we've ever done". The band had written over 50 songs at a farmhouse studio in 2006 first. The Friends EP preceded the album.

eras.title: One bad night in Vancouver, then two careers
eras.text: Gene goes solo and Dean gets a captain's license. Then a January 2011 show in Vancouver goes wrong on stage, and by May 2012 Freeman has told Rolling Stone he's retiring Gene Ween.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Dean Ween
years.h: Gene goes solo and acoustic while Dean earns a captain's license
years.p: Freeman plays as "Gene Ween" alone, then with a band that includes Dave Dreiwitz and drummer Joe Russo. Dean becomes a licensed fishing boat captain.
years.xp: Dean ran a web series called the Brownie Troop Fishing Show and offered trips through Mickey's Guide Service at the Jersey Shore. His captain's license came in 2009 per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Dean Ween at Outside Lands, San Francisco
years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Gene lies on the stage in Vancouver and finishes the show alone
years.p: At the Queen Elizabeth Theatre he sings off-key and lies down during "Superstar"; Dean and Dave Dreiwitz walk off mid-song, and Gene plays the last four songs alone.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia's account, Freeman played tambourine off the beat, sang off-key throughout, and was visibly intoxicated. During "Birthday Boy" Dean and bassist Dreiwitz walked off while Coleman and McClelland swapped instruments. The Seattle show the next night went fine.

Freeman later wrote a song about it, "Covert Discretion": "You don't blow it on stage, lying on your back, screaming nonsense in front of 5,000 people and not try to change something."

years.cap: Gene Ween at Outside Lands, San Francisco
years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Westword: Gene Ween on Ween's history
years.h: Three nights at Denver's Fillmore, and nobody says it's the end
years.p: It's Ween's last show for more than four years. The final song is "The Blarney Stone".
years.xp: Gene wrote "The Blarney Stone" after a day with tattoo artist Joel Rose, a proud Scotsman who showed up with a Scottish sword; they dueled, then Gene went home and wrote it, he told Westword.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Freeman tells Rolling Stone he's retiring Gene Ween
years.p: Dean's reply. Manager Greg Frey announces the split in June, and on July 20 Dean adds that as long as he and Freeman are alive Ween is still together, and quitting is "just laughable".
years.xp: In June, manager Greg Frey told fans on Facebook that Freeman wanted to "more fully explore and pursue his solo career". Freeman's solo album Marvelous Clouds, covers of Rod McKuen songs, had come out about three weeks earlier. Freeman later said he'd left after years of drug and alcohol abuse that got worse on the 2011 tour.

eras.title: Back from the dead, then quiet again
eras.text: Freeman tries a band under his own name, then takes Gene Ween back. The reunion sells out three nights in Colorado and rolls on until Dean steps away from the stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Ween announce a reunion at Broomfield's 1stBank Center
years.p: The first two nights are set for February 12 and 13, 2016. Ticket demand adds a third, February 14.
years.xp: In between, Freeman had formed a five-piece called Freeman, releasing Free-Man in May 2014, and Dean had started the Dean Ween Group. Freeman on taking the name back: "At the end of the day, people know Gene Ween."

years.cap: Ween at the Ryman Auditorium, Nashville
years.src: Westword: Grown, Sober, Still Wild · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Three nights in Broomfield, and no song played twice
years.p: Gene opens with "We're Ween. This is Dean Ween; I'm Gene Ween." The first night runs nearly three hours and over thirty songs.
years.xp: Westword noted Dean was sober. Confetti fell during "Roses Are Free" and Gene said: "We wanted it to be dollar bills." The first night was posted free on Archive.org.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Warner puts out Bananas and Blow without asking the band
years.p: Dean says the song selection on the compilation feels "random".
years.xp: The band found out about it after the fact, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Ween play Red Rocks for South Park's 25th anniversary
years.p: Primus, Trey Parker and Matt Stone share the bill; Comedy Central airs it August 13.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chocolate and Cheese · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Chocolate and Cheese turns 30 with a Bernie Grundman remaster
years.p: Fifteen outtakes and demos come with it. It sells more than 5,000 vinyl copies in its first week and reaches number 15 on Billboard's Top Album Sales.
years.xp: The reissue headlined a 40th-anniversary year that was meant to end with the whole album played at Philadelphia's Mann Center.

years.src: BrooklynVegan: Ween stepping away · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween step away from the stage "for the foreseeable future"
years.p: The band says touring "is too taxing on Deaner's mental health", and the Mann Center show in Philadelphia is canceled.
years.xp: Dean had said in March, when Southeastern dates were canceled, that he needed to "step away from performing live in order to preserve my mental and spiritual well being". Gene said in August he was "perfectly fine and just as disappointed" about the cancellations.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Rhino digs up Europe '90 for Record Store Day
years.p: It pairs a December 25, 1990 studio session, with an early "Push th' Little Daisies", and a live set from Basel, Switzerland. Dean calls the Basel show "the best Ween show of all time".
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, a live album of 1996 Foo Fighters opening dates and reissues of White Pepper and Quebec were announced a week later.
